clue.text: Guard posted near railway

parts.note: posted a letter means sent it

explanation.surface: A guard is stationed close to the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posted' reads as stationed, but it is the past tense of sending mail; 'near' just places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier keeping watch at a post is a guard.

clue.text: Plain description of 9

explanation.surface: A plain account of the puzzle's ninth entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is MUGGINS, a fool, and a fool may be described as simple-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means unadorned or easy; a gullible fool is called simple, meaning naive.

clue.text: Near Main Street, put up entertainment venue

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up reads it from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: main, as in chief, gives top

explanation.surface: Close to the high street, a place of entertainment has been built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like building something, but in a down entry it signals reading the main-street pair from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub or bar visited after dark is a place of entertainment.

clue.text: Held sway, being checked by speaker

indicators.note: a speaker says the word out loud, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: a horse held back with the reins is reined in, or checked

explanation.surface: Someone ruled, but was kept in check by the Speaker of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaker' suggests the parliamentary Speaker, but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold sway is to rule as a monarch does.

clue.text: New collection of recipes when entertaining posh gourmets

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other
the letters of the word recipes are gathered into a new arrangement

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: A fresh recipe book delights refined food lovers at a dinner party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' suggests hosting a dinner, but here it means holding the posh letter inside the reworked recipe letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe people with refined taste in food and drink.

clue.text: Hyde Park character not giving his or her private address?

definitions.text: Hyde Park character not giving his or her private address?

parts.words: Hyde Park character not giving his or her private address?
parts.note: Speakers' Corner in London's Hyde Park is where anyone may stand and harangue a crowd; such an orator's address is a speech to all, not a home address

explanation.surface: A person in a London park won't reveal where they live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' means a speech, not where one lives; Hyde Park is a large London park with Speakers' Corner, a traditional spot for open-air oratory.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator making speeches to the public at Speakers' Corner is the figure described.

clue.text: Greek girl locating pub in centre

indicators.note: the pub goes inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core of something is its centre
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A Greek girl finds a tavern in the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a form of Corinna, from the Greek kore, a maiden.

clue.text: Potato dish I finally left, having swallowed a portion of meat

indicators.note: swallowing something takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other
the letter I at the end is the one that leaves, so it is dropped

parts.note: rosti is a Swiss dish of fried grated potato
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a potato dish after eating a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally left' drops the closing I of ROSTI to leave ROST, and 'having swallowed' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of meat cooked in the oven is a roast.

clue.text: Poet representative of the consumer society?

explanation.surface: A poet who embodies a culture of buying.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Spender was a 20th-century English poet; the second reading is a person who spends.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was an English poet; a big buyer in a shopping culture is one who spends money.

clue.text: Fool put alcoholic drink in large cups

indicators.note: the drink goes inside the word for the cups

parts.note: mugs are large cups
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Some idiot has poured spirits into the coffee mugs.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a gullible person, usually oneself, is this word for a dupe.

clue.text: Jersey crop of little significance?

explanation.surface: A harvest on Jersey that hardly matters.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey, a Channel Island, is famous for its small new potatoes, Jersey Royals; the phrase also means trivial matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey Royals are little new potatoes; things of minor importance are called trivial or insignificant in this idiom.

clue.text: Continuous attack leads to anger among lawyers?

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers
rage is anger

explanation.surface: Fury among the legal profession leads to a sustained assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anger among lawyers' suggests a container, but the pieces simply sit side by side: BAR rage, by analogy with road rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a sustained bombardment of shellfire or questions.

clue.text: Admit Communist has had change of heart

indicators.note: the heart, the central letter of the leader's name, is changed for another

parts.note: Lenin led the Russian Communists

explanation.surface: A Communist confesses to having changed his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the middle N of LENIN for T.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow someone to enter is to admit them.

clue.text: Disaffected by a story Dante translated

parts.note: a story can be a fib, a lie

indicators.note: translating changes the form of something, so the letters of Dante are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader estranged by a translation of Dante's tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' suggests rendering Dante's Italian into English, but it only reorders the five letters of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone estranged or isolated from a group is disaffected.

clue.text: Restless lad, desperate to cover miles in boat

indicators.note: covering something puts it inside, so one piece goes within the other
restless letters will not stay still, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An agitated boy, frantic to travel a long way by water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restless' rearranges LAD and DESPERATE, and 'to cover' places M among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer is a boat driven by paddle wheels.

clue.text: Serviceman eating fish spread

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a marine is a serviceman
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A soldier eating a fish paste sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute spread on bread.

clue.text: Be well-organised, providing vermouth during social gathering

indicators.note: the drink comes in the course of the gathering, so it goes inside

parts.note: a get-together is an informal party
It, short for Italian, is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Be organised, and bring vermouth to the party.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for Italian vermouth comes from the British drink 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort oneself out and act efficiently is the idiom meant.

clue.text: Transplant expert is hard worker

explanation.surface: A surgeon skilled at transplants is industrious.
explanation.walkthrough: A graft is a transplanted piece of tissue or plant; 'graft' is also British slang for hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: One who joins plant or tissue grafts; British slang for a diligent toiler.

clue.text: Ground covered in winter rainstorms

indicators.note: the answer is wrapped inside the letters of these words

explanation.surface: The land was blanketed in winter downpours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' signals the letters lie within 'winTER RAINstorms'.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features.

clue.text: Jazz fan in kind of short trousers

explanation.surface: A jazz lover wearing cut-off trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Hipster was 1940s slang for a jazz devotee; hipsters are trousers cut to sit on the hips, so short in the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A hepcat is a jazz enthusiast; low-waisted trousers that sit on the hips are hipsters.

clue.text: Judge's point of view that has an unpleasant ring

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
an angle is a perspective

explanation.surface: A judge's opinion that sounds wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh metallic ringing noise, like keys shaken, is a discordant sound.

clue.text: Swimmer given warning light by seaman

parts.note: the amber traffic light warns drivers to stop
jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A swimmer is warned by a sailor flashing a light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' means a fish here: the amberjack is a large game fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The amberjack is a sea fish, and fish are swimmers.

clue.text: Tired soldiers accommodated in bunk?

indicators.note: being accommodated in a bed means being put inside it

parts.note: a bunk is a bed
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Exhausted troops were billeted in bunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Weary with boredom, one is tired of something.

clue.text: Town square rebuilt in La Paz

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the letters of La Paz together in a new order

explanation.surface: The main square in the Bolivian city has been reconstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a Spanish-speaking town.

clue.text: Violent storm split apart a party

parts.note: something torn is split apart
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A violent storm broke up a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a whirling, destructive windstorm.

clue.text: Sailor seen round stern of boat, hunting for vermin

indicators.note: the sailor is seen going round the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a rating is a sailor without a commission

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a boat, so its last letter

explanation.surface: A sailor at the back of a boat is chasing pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern of' gives T, the last letter of 'boat', which goes inside RATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching rats, as terriers do, is hunting pests.

clue.text: Strangely endures singular display of bad manners

indicators.note: the letters of endures are arranged in a strange new way

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Someone oddly puts up with a remarkable show of impoliteness.
explanation.definitionFit: Impoliteness shown to others is ill manners.

clue.text: French cheeses said to give you wind

indicators.note: said tells us the word is spoken, so a homophone is wanted

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Eating French cheese gives you gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' points to flatulence in the surface but means a light wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is a gentle current of moving air.
